newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-Firm oil price to lift BP Q3 profit.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Firm oil price to lift BP Q3 profit.

text.p: Strong oil price will have fuelled third quarter results for British Petroleum Co Plc, which reports on Tuesday, analysts said.
The BP figures will come after Royal Dutch/Shell on Thursday disappointed the stock market with lower earnings.
But BP relies less than the Anglo-Dutch giant on poor refining and bulk chemicals markets and will therefore benefit more higher production results due to the strong crude price.
Analysts' forecast for net earnings on a replacement cost basis vary between 600-675 million stg, up from 532 million a year ago.
But analysts also warn for too much optimism over the exploration and production result.
They note that BP's operations for a large part depend on Alaskan crude, which lags Brent prices by about a month and actually weakened in the third quarter.

Nick Antill at BZW sees exploration and production profits up by 200 million stg from 527 million stg, refining and marketing down by 15 million from 161 million and chemical profit may fall by 110 million from 225 million.
Third quarter Brent crude prices were an average $21 barrel, which was about a dollar higher than in the second quarter and well over four dollars more than in the same 1995 period.

Industry watchers say oil prices may retreat in the medium term, although there might be a sudden spike up following any cold spell. Most expect crude to trade at an average of somewhat below $20 per barrel in 1997.
This more subdued scenario is seen offering little for problems for BP, which is set to profit next year from several bold rationalisation measures taken in 1995.
Analysts hope the third quarter results will be accompanied by statements on the planned sale of two refineries and progress on the European downstream merger with Mobil.

Mobil and BP have said they expected the link-up to results in costs savings of up to 500 million stg a year. But there have been several suggestions in the media that this figure could be easily exceeded. The refineries at Lavera in France and Lima in Ohio were put up for sale in January and BP indicated in August they may actually be sold before the end of the year.
"There still is quite some upward potential in BP," said Jurjen Lunshof at Credit Lyonnais Laing.
